label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=7)
explanation: Fires almost only on the delimiter step (97% of activation mass; never in the copy phase, apart from a trickle on the last 1-2 original tokens of L=8-9 sequences). Within <DEL> steps it is graded and only crosses threshold on about 12% of them. Rate and magnitude grow strongly with sequence length (L<=5 ~0, L=7 ~0.9x, L=9 ~1.9x lift; t=9 carries 48% of mass). It also depends on the first original token, which is the token about to be output: digits 0/1/2 and letters z/h/j/n give the highest rates. Sequences with more digits fire more often. Restricting to these first tokens raises precision to ~0.5-0.6 but halves recall, so the token preference is graded rather than a clean gate. The predicate covers 95% of mass but has low precision (~0.23) because most long-sequence <DEL> steps stay below threshold.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: 0, 1, 2, z, j, h; least: s, f, p, d) and the next token to output (most: 0, 2, h, 1, z, m; least: a, s, f, p); timing cues that raise it most: t=7, L=9 & t=7, t=8.
